chapters.title: Welcome: Modules Home and the Dashboard
chapters.goal: Find your way around HCC: the Modules Home tiles, the top bar, search, the menu, Appearance & display and the Dashboard.

steps.say: This is Modules Home, the first screen after you choose your name. Each tile is one module; the red number on a tile is the work waiting there.
steps.why: Everything in HCC starts from these tiles, and you only see the modules your role may use.
steps.expect: Nine module tiles for Reception: Front Desk, Cash & Billing, Housekeeping & Maintenance, Guests & Services, Customers, Revenue & Sales, People & Payroll, Accounts & Reports, Admin & Setup.

steps.say: Look at the top bar. It shows the business date, whether the day is Open, the hotel clock, and who is signed in: Aarav, Reception.
steps.why: Every entry you make carries this business date and your name, so check them before you start work.
steps.expect: Business date 24 Oct 2026, Open, 08:00 IST, Aarav · Reception.

steps.say: Click the Front Desk tile to open that module.
steps.why: A module page lists its screens as tiles; the number on the tile shows open work.
steps.expect: The Front Desk page opens with tiles such as Room board, Calendar, Reservations, Guests, Arrivals & check-in and Room keys.

steps.say: Look at the breadcrumb at the top left, Modules Home then Front Desk. Click Modules Home to go back.
steps.why: The breadcrumb always shows where you are, and every earlier part of it is a link.
steps.expect: You are back on Modules Home.

steps.say: Press Control and K, or click the Search button in the top bar, to open the search box.
steps.why: Search is the quickest way to any screen, and it also offers quick actions: New reservation, Walk-in guest and Add expense.
steps.expect: The search box opens with the three quick actions and the popular pages.

steps.say: Type part of a name, for example rates. The list narrows as you type.
steps.why: You only see pages your role may open, so a search never leads to a screen you cannot use.
steps.expect: Pages and actions that match the word.

steps.say: Press Escape to close the search box without choosing anything.
steps.why: Escape closes any dialog in HCC and leaves your work as it was.

steps.say: Click the menu button at the top left to open the side menu.
steps.why: The side menu lists every module and page in the same order as the tiles, and has Change my PIN and Sign out.
steps.expect: The side menu opens with Modules Home, the module list, Demo & display, Change my PIN and Sign out.

steps.say: Close the menu, then open Admin & Setup, Appearance & display. Here each person sets text size, theme and start page for this device.
steps.why: These choices belong to this device only. They are not hotel data and they are not audited.
steps.expect: The Appearance & display page opens: text size, theme, density, motion, start page, list size and message time.

steps.say: Meera, the Manager, also sees a Dashboard tile that Reception does not have. Click Dashboard to see the day at a glance.
steps.why: The Dashboard gives the manager the day's occupancy, arrivals, cash and open work on one screen.
steps.expect: The Dashboard page opens for Meera (Manager).

chapters.title: Reservations and the Calendar
chapters.goal: Take a booking for Mr. Rahul Deshmukh, hold a room for an enquiry, book a company guest, read the Calendar and cancel a booking.

steps.say: You are Aarav at Reception, on Modules Home. This chapter takes bookings, so you will work in the Front Desk module.
steps.why: Choose the module first, then the screen.

steps.say: Click the Front Desk tile.
steps.why: Reservations, the Calendar, check-in and the room board all live in this module.

steps.say: Click the Reservations tile.
steps.why: This list holds every booking, past and future.
steps.expect: The Reservations page opens with all bookings.

steps.say: Read the list. Each row shows the guest, booking number, room, stay dates, status, advance paid and folio balance.
steps.why: Reception checks this list before telling a caller whether a booking exists.
steps.expect: The list of all bookings, newest first.

steps.say: Click the Held chip to see only bookings that are on hold.
steps.why: A hold keeps a room for a short time while the guest decides. Held, Expired, Confirmed, In house, Departed, Cancelled and No show each have a chip.

steps.say: Click All, then type a guest name in the search box. Type Ghate.
steps.why: Search finds a booking by guest name, phone number, room number or booking number.
steps.expect: Only bookings of guests named Ghate are listed.

steps.say: Clear the search box to see all bookings again.
steps.why: An old search left in the box hides bookings and confuses the next person.

steps.say: Click New reservation to take a booking.
steps.why: A reservation reserves a room before the guest arrives.

steps.say: The dialog opens with Arrival 24 Oct 2026 and Departure 26 Oct 2026. Rahul Deshmukh stays two nights, so leave the dates as they are.
steps.why: The dates decide the room rate, the tax and the availability list below.

steps.say: Choose 2 adults. Rahul travels with Mrs. Sneha Deshmukh.
steps.why: The number of guests limits which room types can be booked.

steps.say: Choose the room type Deluxe.
steps.why: The list of rooms below shows only the rooms that are free for these dates.
steps.expect: Only free Deluxe rooms are listed.

steps.say: Choose room 203, Deluxe, Rs 3,000 a night.
steps.why: Auto-assign would pick the first free room. Rahul asked for 203, so choose it yourself.

steps.say: Type the guest name: Rahul Deshmukh.
steps.why: The name on the booking is printed on the registration card and the invoice.

steps.say: Type the mobile number. The training uses a dummy number.
steps.why: The phone number is how reception reaches the guest and finds the booking again.

steps.say: Choose the booking source Phone, because Rahul booked by calling the hotel.
steps.why: The source feeds the reports on where bookings come from.

steps.say: Type the notes: wake-up call at 06:30 on 25 October and two extra towels.
steps.why: Notes travel with the booking so the night staff and housekeeping can see the guest's requests.
steps.value: Wake-up call 06:30 on 25 Oct. Two extra towels.
auto: type:field:Notes|Wake-up call 06:30 on 25 Oct. Two extra towels.

steps.say: Click Confirm reservation.
steps.why: Confirm keeps the room for the guest. Use Hold 2 hours instead when the guest has not decided yet.
steps.expect: The reservation is confirmed as HCC-1101 and its booking dialog opens.
steps.msgText: Reservation confirmed. Open it to register the guest and check in.

steps.say: The booking dialog opens for HCC-1101: Rahul Deshmukh, room 203, 24 to 26 October, Confirmed. The buttons are the actions you can take from here.
steps.why: From this dialog reception changes, cancels, prints and checks in the booking.
steps.expect: The booking dialog with the folio and the action buttons.

steps.say: Click Change dates / room to see how a booking is amended.
steps.why: Guests change plans; the booking can be moved without cancelling it.
steps.expect: The Move / change dates view opens inside the dialog.

steps.say: Change nothing. Click Back.
steps.why: Back returns to the booking without saving anything.
steps.expect: The booking dialog is shown again.

steps.say: Press Escape to close the booking dialog.
steps.why: Escape closes any dialog and leaves the data as it was.

steps.say: Now an enquiry: Mrs. Meena Kulkarni phones but has not decided. Click New reservation.
steps.why: A hold stops another guest taking the room while she decides.
steps.expect: A new, empty reservation dialog opens.

steps.say: Enter her name and phone, then set Arrival 28 Oct and Departure 30 Oct.
steps.why: Always enter dates first, because only rooms free on those dates are offered.
steps.expect: Name, phone and the new dates are filled.

steps.say: Click Hold 2 hours.
steps.why: The room is kept for two hours. If nobody confirms it, the hold lapses by itself and shows under Expired.
steps.expect: The booking is saved as Held.

steps.say: Before booking a company guest, the company needs an account with a credit limit, and only the Owner may set a limit. Sagar, the Owner, opens Revenue & Sales, Groups, the Companies tab and clicks New company.
steps.why: A company account lets the hotel bill the company later. Reception asks the Owner for it; reception cannot book a company on credit without one.
steps.expect: The New company account dialog opens.

steps.say: Type the company name Shree Agro Industries, the fictional GSTIN 27AABCS1234A1Z5 and the opening credit limit 50,000 rupees.
steps.why: The credit limit stops the company running up more than the hotel agreed to carry.

steps.say: Click Create account.
steps.why: The company now appears in the booking form and in Accounting as a party.

steps.say: Back at Reception, Aarav books Mr. Vikram Jadhav of Shree Agro Industries: Suite 106 from 24 to 25 October, billed to the company account. Open Reservations, click New reservation and fill the form.
steps.why: The company guest does not pay at check-out; the folio goes to the company account.
steps.expect: The form shows Vikram Jadhav, Suite 106, 24 to 25 October, billed to Shree Agro Industries.

steps.say: Click Confirm reservation.
steps.why: A company booking is confirmed like any other; only the billing differs.
steps.expect: The booking for Vikram Jadhav is confirmed.

steps.say: Press Escape to close the booking dialog.
steps.why: You will check Vikram in later, with the other arrivals.

steps.say: Open the Calendar from Front Desk. Each row is a room and each column a night; coloured bars are bookings.
steps.why: The Calendar shows at a glance which rooms are free on which nights.
steps.expect: The Calendar opens, 24 Oct to 6 Nov.

steps.say: Click Next week to move the window forward a week.
steps.why: The grid shows two weeks at a time; the arrows move it.
steps.expect: The window now starts a week later.

steps.say: Click Today to come back to the business date.
steps.why: Today always returns to 24 Oct 2026, the business date.
steps.expect: The window starts at 24 Oct again.

steps.say: Click an empty cell, for example room 105 from 26 Oct, to start a booking for that room and night.
steps.why: This is the quickest way to book when you are looking at the grid.
steps.expect: The New reservation dialog opens for room 105 from 26 Oct.

steps.say: Press Escape to leave without booking.
steps.why: Nothing is saved until you click Confirm or Hold.

steps.say: Mrs. Kulkarni calls back to cancel. Open Reservations, search booking HCC-1103 and open it.
steps.why: Search by booking number is exact, so you never open the wrong guest.
steps.expect: The booking dialog for the held booking opens.

steps.say: A held booking has Confirm hold when the guest agrees and Cancel hold when she does not. A confirmed booking has Cancel / no-show instead; if money is held on it, refund the advance first.
steps.why: Knowing which button belongs to which status saves a wrong click.
steps.expect: The held booking dialog with Confirm hold and Cancel hold.

steps.say: Click Cancel hold. Mrs. Kulkarni does not want the rooms.
steps.why: A hold is cancelled in two clicks so that nobody cancels one by mistake.
steps.expect: A confirmation asks you to confirm the cancellation.

steps.say: Click Cancel hold again to confirm.
steps.why: Cancelling a hold frees the room at once; the booking stays in the list as Cancelled for the record.
steps.expect: The hold is cancelled and the room is free again.

chapters.title: Arrivals, registration and check-in
chapters.goal: Check in Mr. Rahul Deshmukh with a verified ID and an advance, walk in Ms. Anita Rao, find a guest profile, capture IDs and issue a room key.

steps.say: Rahul Deshmukh has arrived. You are Aarav on Modules Home; check-in starts in the Front Desk module.
steps.why: Check-in is the most important job at the front desk: it ties the guest, the ID and the room together.

steps.say: Click the Front Desk tile.
steps.why: Arrivals, guests, keys and documents are all front-desk screens.

steps.say: Click the Arrivals & check-in tile.
steps.why: This screen lists everyone expected today.

steps.say: Four bookings are expected today: Ishaan Bose, Vikram Jadhav, Rahul Deshmukh and Aditi Nair. The list shows the registration status, the room status and the advance paid.
steps.why: You see at a glance whether the room is ready and whether the guest is already registered.

steps.say: Type the booking number HCC-1101 in the search box. The box also accepts a name, a room or a vehicle number.
steps.why: A booking number is the surest way to find the right guest.

steps.say: Click Start check-in on Rahul's row.
steps.why: The guided check-in takes you through six steps, so nothing is forgotten.
steps.expect: The guided check-in opens at the registration step.

steps.say: Step 2 of 6 is the registration card. The name and phone come from the booking; address and ID are still empty.
steps.why: The law requires a verified identity for every guest, so the room cannot be given until this step is done.

steps.say: Type the address from the guest's ID: 12 Karve Road, Pune 411004.
steps.why: The address is printed on the registration card and the invoice.

steps.say: Choose the ID type Aadhaar.
steps.why: Each ID type has its own number check; Aadhaar needs exactly twelve digits with a valid check digit.

steps.say: Type the Aadhaar number from the card. The training uses a fictional number that passes the check.
steps.why: After saving, HCC shows the number masked, XXXX XXXX 4321, to everyone except those who may view it.

steps.say: Click Verify registration.
steps.why: The registration is saved and the guest is marked Verified.

steps.say: Room 203 is vacant and ready, so it is eligible. Click Continue.
steps.why: A dirty or blocked room cannot be given; HCC would say why on this step.

steps.say: Read the tariff to the guest, Rs 3,000 a night for 2 nights, and tick that the guest confirmed it.
steps.why: Rate disputes at check-out are avoided when the guest agreed at check-in.

steps.say: Click Continue.
steps.why: Next is the advance. It is optional here.

steps.say: Rahul pays Rs 2,000 as advance. Click Record advance / deposit.
steps.why: An advance is money received before the stay; it is kept on the booking and counted against the final bill.

steps.say: Type the amount 2000.
steps.why: Amounts are entered in rupees and stored exactly.

steps.say: Choose the method UPI.
steps.why: The method decides which cashier total the money joins: cash, UPI, card or bank transfer.

steps.say: Type the UPI reference number from the guest's phone.
steps.why: The reference lets the accountant match the receipt with the bank statement.

steps.say: Click Review.
steps.why: Review shows the balance after posting before anything is saved.
steps.expect: A summary of the receipt is shown.

steps.say: Click Post receipt.
steps.why: Posting a receipt twice is blocked; a repeated click never creates a second receipt.
steps.expect: The receipt is recorded and the booking dialog is shown.

steps.say: Click Guided check-in to continue where you stopped.
steps.why: Completed steps are remembered from the record.

steps.say: Tick the tariff confirmation again and click Continue twice to reach step 6, Check in.
steps.why: The tick belongs to this session; the advance step is complete now.
steps.expect: Step 6 of 6, Check in, with the stay details.

steps.say: Choose the purpose of visit: Business.
steps.why: The purpose of visit is part of the legal guest record.

steps.say: Type the car number MH 12 AB 1234.
steps.why: The vehicle number helps parking and can be searched on this screen.

steps.say: Click Check in.
steps.why: Check-in makes the guest in-house and updates the room board to Occupied.
steps.expect: Rahul Deshmukh is checked in to room 203.
steps.msgText: Checked in to room 203. Room board updated.

steps.say: Click Registration card to see the card the guest signs.
steps.why: The card carries the hotel letterhead, the stay, the guests and the masked ID.

steps.say: This is the registration card of Rahul Deshmukh, with the accompanying guests and the masked ID. Print it, or save a PDF, and let the guest sign.
steps.why: A signed card is the proof of registration.

steps.say: Close the card and the dialog, then open Walk-in on the Arrivals page for a guest without a booking.
steps.why: A walk-in guest is registered and checked in in one step.

steps.say: Ms. Anita Rao from Hyderabad has no booking. Type her name, phone and address.
steps.why: The same registration rules apply to a walk-in.

steps.say: Choose ID type Aadhaar and type her fictional number 345678901238.
steps.why: The ID is checked before the guest can be checked in.

steps.say: Choose room 105, Classic, for one night and the purpose Tourism.
steps.why: Only rooms that are vacant, ready and free for the whole stay are offered.

steps.say: Click Create walk-in and check in.
steps.why: HCC creates the booking, registers the guest and checks her in. Anita pays her bill at the cashier.
steps.expect: Anita Rao is checked in to room 105.

steps.say: Open Guests from Front Desk and search for Deshmukh. This is the guest register.
steps.why: The register keeps one profile per guest, with every stay.
steps.expect: Guests named Rahul Deshmukh are listed.

steps.say: Click Rahul Deshmukh, profile G-1110.
steps.why: The profile shows his contact details, the accompanying guests, photos and the stay history.
steps.expect: The profile opens on the right.

steps.say: Open Document capture under Guests & Services. Here a scanned ID or bill is filed against a guest.
steps.why: Scanning is simulated in the demo; on a real PC the scanner or camera sends the picture here.

steps.say: Key cards are made from the booking. Open the booking of Rahul in Reservations and click Room key.
steps.why: The key belongs to the stay, so it is made from the booking of the stay.
steps.expect: The room key panel opens for room 203 and says the key service is offline.

steps.say: The panel says the encoder is offline. In the training, Meera, the Manager, brings the simulated encoder online on the Room keys page, Encoder tab.
steps.why: Only a manager can switch the encoder. In the real hotel the Key Agent beside the front-desk PC does this by itself.

steps.say: Back at Reception, open the room key panel again and click Issue key to make the card for room 203.
steps.why: The request goes to the encoder at the front desk, which writes the card.
steps.expect: A key request is sent and shown as waiting.

steps.say: At the encoder, the job runs. In the training Meera clicks Finish job on the Encoder tab.
steps.why: When the card is written the job turns to Done and the card is listed under Active cards.

steps.say: Suppose the guest loses the card. Open the room key panel and click Lost card.
steps.why: A lost card is cancelled and a new one issued, so the old card cannot open the door.

steps.say: Click Finish job again on the Encoder tab to write the new card.
steps.why: The old card is cancelled; only the new card opens room 203.

steps.say: Open the Key log tab. It lists every key action with its time, room and user.
steps.why: The log lets the manager see who made which card and when.
steps.expect: The key log shows the issue and the re-issue for room 203.

chapters.title: The Room board
chapters.goal: Read the Room board: status colours, filters, floors, the room drawer, and how a manager blocks and unblocks a room.

steps.say: You are Aarav on Modules Home. The Room board is the screen the front desk looks at most often.
steps.why: It shows every room and its state right now.

steps.say: Click the Front Desk tile.
steps.why: The Room board is the first tile of the module.

steps.say: Click the Room board tile.
steps.why: The board opens on all floors.

steps.say: Every room is a card with its number, type, guest or housekeeping state and the date it is busy until. Rahul Deshmukh is in 203, Anita Rao in 105.
steps.why: You can tell at a glance who is in which room and when they leave.

steps.say: The chips Occupied, Ready, Dirty, Cleaning, Inspection and Blocked filter the board. Ready means clean and sold-ready; Dirty needs cleaning; Inspection waits for the supervisor.
steps.why: Colours always come with a word, so the board is readable without colour.

steps.say: Click the Dirty chip to see only rooms that need cleaning.
steps.why: This is the list housekeeping works from.

steps.say: Click All to see every room again.
steps.why: Always return to All; an old filter hides rooms from the next person.

steps.say: Click Floor 2 to see only the second floor.
steps.why: The floor tabs help on a busy day.

steps.say: Click All floors to see the whole hotel.
steps.why: The tab shows the number of rooms on each floor.

steps.say: Click room 203 to open its drawer.
steps.why: The drawer shows who is in the room and what can be done from here.
steps.expect: The Room 203 drawer opens with the guest Rahul Deshmukh.

steps.say: The drawer lists the guest and the stay, 24 Oct to 26 Oct, and a Report repair button. Reception cannot block a room; that is a manager's decision.
steps.why: A blocked room is removed from sale, so only people responsible for stock may do it.

steps.say: Meera, the Manager, opens room 108 on the Room board and clicks Block for repair. Room 108 is dirty and needs a deep clean.
steps.why: A block takes the room out of sale until it is lifted.
steps.expect: The Block for repair form opens.

steps.say: Type the reason: Deep clean.
steps.why: The reason is kept in the room history so everyone knows why the room is off sale.

steps.say: Click Block room.
steps.why: From today the room cannot be booked or given to a guest.

steps.say: When the deep clean is finished, open room 108 again and click Unblock room.
steps.why: Unblocking returns the room to the normal housekeeping flow.
steps.expect: The drawer for 108 shows Change block and Unblock room.

steps.say: Click Unblock room.
steps.why: Housekeeping then cleans and inspects the room as usual.

chapters.title: In-house guests and guest services
chapters.goal: Look after Rahul Deshmukh while he stays: in-house list, requests, wake-up call, a complaint, a room move, reminders and messages.

steps.say: Rahul is in room 203. You are Aarav on Modules Home; everything for guests who are staying lives under Guests & Services.
steps.why: A good stay is made of small requests handled on time.

steps.say: Click the Guests & Services tile.
steps.why: It holds in-house stays, guest requests, messages and document capture.

steps.say: Click the In-house stays tile.
steps.why: This is the list of every guest in the hotel now.

steps.say: The list shows each in-house room with the guest, booking number, stay dates and the balance. Find room 203, Rahul Deshmukh.
steps.why: The balance column tells reception who still owes money before check-out.

steps.say: Click the row of room 203.
steps.why: The details of the stay open on the right: room segments, occupants and the folio summary.
steps.expect: The details of the stay HCC-1101 open.

steps.say: Click Extend / shorten to see how the departure date is changed.
steps.why: A guest who stays longer or leaves early is handled here, with the folio and the room kept in step.
steps.expect: The Extend / shorten tab shows the departure date.

steps.say: Press Escape. Rahul keeps his dates, so change nothing.
steps.why: The Leaves today tab next to it starts an early check-out.

steps.say: Open Guest services under Guests & Services and click New request. Rahul asks for two extra towels.
steps.why: Every request is logged so that it is done, timed and not forgotten.

steps.say: Choose Room 203, Rahul Deshmukh, and the request Extra towels. Assign it to Ravi.
steps.why: The assignee gets the request on his phone; the priority decides how fast it must be done.
steps.expect: Room 203, Extra towels, assigned to Ravi.

steps.say: Click Log request.
steps.why: The request starts its service clock now.

steps.say: Rahul also wants a wake-up call at 06:30 on 25 October. Click New request, choose Room 203, the request Wake-up call and type the time in Detail.
steps.why: A wake-up request is a promise; the night desk calls at the time given.
steps.expect: A wake-up request for room 203 at 06:30.

steps.say: Click Log request.
steps.why: The wake-up now appears on the Wake-ups list of Reminders & wake-ups.

steps.say: Rahul calls at night: the air conditioner is noisy. Open the Complaints tab.
steps.why: A complaint is different from a request: it needs an owner and a follow-up.

steps.say: Click Log complaint.
steps.why: The dialog links the complaint to the stay.

steps.say: Link it to Room 203, choose the category Maintenance, severity Medium, and describe what happened.
steps.why: The category sends the complaint to the right team; the severity decides how quickly the manager must act.
auto: type:field:What happened|Air conditioner in room 203 is noisy at night

steps.say: Click Log complaint.
steps.why: You will turn this into a work order for the maintenance team later, and offer the guest a service-recovery discount on the folio.

steps.say: Open the Lost & found tab.
steps.why: Anything a guest leaves behind is logged here with the room and the finder; housekeeping adds the entries, reception returns the items.

steps.say: The next day the air conditioner is still faulty, so Rahul is moved. Open In-house stays, open room 203 and click Move room.
steps.why: A move keeps the booking, the folio and the guest history; only the room changes.

steps.say: The dialog offers rooms that are free and ready: 107 Deluxe (same type), 205 Classic and 306 Suite. Room 207 in the plan is reserved for an arrival today, so the training uses 107.
steps.why: Giving the same room type avoids a rate change; a cheaper or dearer type needs the rate rule explained to the guest.

steps.say: Click Move to 107.
steps.why: The old room goes to housekeeping as dirty and the room board changes at once.

steps.say: Ravi, the room attendant, sees the towel request on his phone-style page My guest requests. Open it as Ravi.
steps.why: Housekeepers see only their own requests and no money.
steps.expect: My guest requests lists the towels for room 203.

steps.say: Click Start when you take the request.
steps.why: Start stops the waiting time and starts the work time.

steps.say: Click Complete when the towels are delivered.
steps.why: Completing closes the request and records the service time against the target.

steps.say: Type a short note for the guest: Two towels delivered to the room. Then click Mark done.
steps.why: The note is what the guest and the desk read later.
auto: type:field:Note for the guest|Two towels delivered to the room

steps.say: Back at Reception, open Reminders & wake-ups under Front Desk and click New reminder.
steps.why: Reminders are notes with a date that the desk sees on the day.

steps.say: Type the subject Collect ID copy from 206, keep today's date and the alert of 3 days.
steps.why: The alert days make the reminder show earlier, so it is not missed.

steps.say: Click Save reminder.
steps.why: The reminder appears on the desk list today and as a banner until it is done.

steps.say: Open the Wake-ups tab.
steps.why: All wake-up calls of the day are listed; the night desk marks each as done after calling.

steps.say: Open Messages under Guests & Services. The Outbox lists every message sent to guests; click Compose.
steps.why: Messages are queued here; sending is simulated in the demo, so no real WhatsApp, SMS or e-mail leaves the hotel.

steps.say: Choose the guest Rahul Deshmukh, the channel WhatsApp and the template Booking confirmation.
steps.why: A template fills the text with the guest's name and booking details.
steps.expect: The message text is filled from the template.

steps.say: Click Queue message.
steps.why: The message waits in the Outbox. A guest who has not given consent receives nothing.
steps.expect: The message is in the Outbox.

steps.say: Click Simulate delivery to play the delivery of the queued messages.
steps.why: In the real hotel the messaging service delivers; here the demo shows what would happen.

steps.say: Open the Consent tab.
steps.why: Guests must agree before they get marketing or service messages; HCC keeps the record.

steps.say: Open the Templates tab.
steps.why: Templates are the standard texts of the hotel; the owner and manager can edit them.
steps.expect: The six message templates are listed.

steps.say: Open the Triggers tab.
steps.why: A trigger is a rule: for example send a welcome message at check-in or a feedback request after check-out.
steps.expect: The seven message rules are listed.

chapters.title: The folio: charges, discounts and corrections
chapters.goal: Open the folio of Rahul Deshmukh, post a laundry charge and a free-text charge, set the meal plan, see how a discount and a rate change go through approval.

steps.say: You are Priya, the cashier, on Modules Home. The folio is the guest's running account: everything the guest owes and has paid.
steps.why: Every rupee a guest pays or owes goes through the folio.

steps.say: Click the Cash & Billing tile.
steps.why: Folios, the cashier shift, the cash book, restaurant checks and expenses are here.

steps.say: Click the Guests & folios tile.
steps.why: This is the list of every guest bill.

steps.say: The chips All, In house, Due out, Balance due, Departed and Confirmed filter the list. Folio requests lists requests waiting for approval.
steps.why: Cashiers use Due out and Balance due to prepare check-outs.

steps.say: Type the booking number HCC-1101.

steps.why: The request goes to Meera.

steps.say: Meera opens Staff & payroll, the Leave tab and its Approvals. She approves Kavya's request.
steps.why: The approver sees the entitlement left and how many are on leave that day before agreeing.
steps.expect: The leave approvals list shows Approve and Reject.

steps.say: Click Approve on Kavya's request.
steps.why: The quota is checked again at approval; the leave appears on the calendar and in the payroll days.

steps.say: Sagar, the Owner, opens the Payroll tab. The months April to September are locked runs.
steps.why: Payroll is the Owner's screen: pay days come from the attendance and the leave.
steps.expect: The monthly payroll register opens on September.

steps.say: Each row is one employee with the pay days, the earnings, the PF, ESIC and professional-tax deductions and the net pay. The month is locked; Unlock reopens it for a correction. Register CSV and Excel, the bank transfer file and the PF / ESIC / PT statement are exports for the accountant and the bank. October cannot be run yet, because a month is processed after it ends.
steps.why: A locked month cannot be changed by mistake.

steps.say: Click Payslip on a row.
steps.why: The payslip is the printout the employee takes home.

steps.say: Close the payslip and open the Advances tab. Click Record advance for the new attendant Sunil Pawar. Ravi already has an open advance, and HCC allows one open advance per person.
steps.why: A salary advance is paid now and recovered from the next payroll.

steps.say: Choose the staff member Sunil Pawar, the amount 2000 rupees, recovery from October 2026 payroll, paid from drawer cash, and the reason Festival advance.
steps.why: The advance is recovered automatically, so the payroll needs no manual calculation.

steps.say: Click Record advance.
steps.why: The cash leaves the drawer and the amount shows against Sunil until recovered.

steps.say: Open the Full and final tab.
steps.why: When a person leaves, the final settlement of pay, leave and advances is worked out here; nobody is leaving today.
steps.expect: The page says nobody is waiting for a settlement.

steps.say: Open the Statutory rates tab.
steps.why: PF, ESIC and professional-tax rates are versioned, so an old payroll is never recalculated with a new rate.
steps.expect: The statutory rate versions are listed.

steps.say: Ravi opens People & Payroll. He sees only My shifts & pay: today's shift, his week, his leave balance and his payslip.
steps.why: Staff see only their own pay; housekeeping and maintenance see no hotel money.
steps.expect: My shifts & pay opens for Ravi.

steps.say: The page shows the Morning shift 07:00 to 15:00, a Check in now button for attendance, the week, the month so far, the leave quota of the financial year and the payslip of September with View / print and Payslip PDF.
steps.why: This page is on the phone for every employee.

chapters.title: Day close
chapters.goal: Walk the seven steps of the Day closing page: preflight, room nights, the cash shift, closing, the summary, the next day and corrections. The demo day cannot close because ten stays are due out.

steps.say: It is 26 October. Meera, the Manager, is on Modules Home. At the end of every day she closes the business date.
steps.why: Closing the day freezes the figures of the day, posts the room nights and opens the next date.

steps.say: Click the Accounts & Reports tile.
steps.why: Day closing, reports, accounting, compliance and the assistant are here.

steps.say: Click the Day closing tile.
steps.why: The page leads you through the close in order.

steps.say: The page shows the current business date, 26 Oct 2026, and seven steps: 1 Preflight, 2 Post room nights, 3 Cash shift, 4 Close business date, 5 Closing summary, 6 Open next business day, 7 Reopen & corrections. Each shows its state: done, current step, waiting or blocked.
steps.why: The order cannot be skipped, so the close is always complete.

steps.say: Click 1. Preflight.
steps.why: The preflight lists everything that must be settled before the day can close.

steps.say: Arrivals, expired holds, approvals, expenses and restaurant checks are all clear. One check is blocked: Overdue departures resolved, ten guests are due out today, from Ananya Rao in room 101 to Aditi Nair in room 207. Each must be settled and checked out, or the stay extended.
steps.why: A guest who should have left must be dealt with, so the room is not sold twice.
steps.expect: The blocked check lists ten guests.

steps.say: Click 2. Post room nights.
steps.why: The night audit posts one room charge for every in-house stay; it is safe to run twice.
steps.expect: The step shows that room nights are posted.

steps.say: Click Preview report.
steps.why: The preview shows the closing report as it would be, without closing the day.

steps.say: Close the preview. Priya counts the drawer on the Cashier shift page. The expected cash is Rs 9,625; she types the counted amount.
steps.why: The shift must be counted and closed before the day can close; a difference needs a reason.

steps.say: With the count equal to the expected cash the Difference box shows zero, and Submit count & close shift would close the shift. A difference needs a reason and the approval of another user. The training does not submit here, because the Cashier shift page and the close command disagree on the expected cash in this demo (see TRAINING_NOTES).
steps.why: The shift must be closed before the day can close.
steps.expect: The count form with a zero difference.

steps.say: Meera opens Day closing again. Step 3, Cash shift, still waits for the close of the shift; step 4 is blocked by the ten overdue departures.
steps.why: Close business date stays grey until every check is green.

steps.say: Click 4. Close business date.
steps.why: The Close button names the date, Close 26 Oct, and is available only when nothing blocks it.
steps.expect: The reasons that block the close are listed.

steps.say: Click 5. Closing summary.
steps.why: After the close, the summary shows net receipts, cash, tax and the room figures of the day.
steps.expect: The closing summary preview is shown.

steps.say: Click 6. Open next business day.
steps.why: After the close, Open next business day moves the date to 27 Oct and carries the cash forward; each cashier opens a new shift.
steps.expect: The step shows the next date, 27 Oct, waiting for the close.

steps.say: Click 7. Reopen & corrections.
steps.why: If an error is found after the close, the Owner can reopen the day with a reason; HCC records every reopening and closes the day again.
steps.expect: The reopening step shows nothing reopened.

steps.say: To finish the training day, each of the ten guests would be checked out as in chapter 8 and the day closed with the Close 26 Oct button. The demo does not do this, so the data of the next chapters stays on 26 October.
steps.why: The close is the last job of every day; the owner reads its result in the digest next morning.

chapters.title: Reports and the Report hub
chapters.goal: Read the Reports page, choose a period, find reports in the library, mark favourites, see scheduled runs and the export log, and read revenue by category and the owner digest.

steps.say: Meera, the Manager, is on Modules Home. All figures of the hotel come out of the Accounts & Reports module.
steps.why: A manager decides with figures, not with memory.

steps.say: Click the Accounts & Reports tile.
steps.why: Reports, the report library, revenue by category and the owner digest are listed here.

steps.say: Click the Reports tile.
steps.why: This page gives the standard reports for a period.

steps.say: At the top are the period buttons Today, Last 3 days, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month and FY history, and the From and To dates. Below are the report names: Daily operations, Revenue & tax, Receipts & deposits, Expenses & cash, Occupancy and the Report dictionary.
steps.why: Every report has a period, so the same report serves a day and a month.
steps.expect: The period buttons and the report names.

steps.say: Click Last 7 days.
steps.why: The dates and every figure change at once.
steps.expect: The period is the last seven days.

steps.say: Click Revenue & tax.
steps.why: This report shows the room and food revenue with the GST split.
steps.expect: The revenue and tax report opens.

steps.say: Each report can be exported as CSV or Excel, or printed. The source rows behind every figure open with the view link, so a total can always be traced to the bills.
steps.why: A figure that cannot be traced is not trusted.

steps.say: Click Report dictionary.
steps.why: The dictionary explains every figure: what it counts and what it leaves out.

steps.say: Open Report library under Accounts & Reports. It lists every report by group: Guests, Rooms, Money & cash and Tax & GST.
steps.why: The library has more reports than the Reports page, with search and favourites.

steps.say: Type cash in the search box.
steps.why: The list narrows to reports with that word.

steps.say: Click Add to favourites on Cash book.
steps.why: A favourite stays at the top of your list on your own login.
steps.expect: The Cash book is a favourite.

steps.say: Tick Favourites only.
steps.why: Your daily reports are one click away.

steps.say: Open the Scheduled runs tab.
steps.why: A report can be scheduled to run every morning and be sent to the owner; a schedule runs with the rights of the person who made it.

steps.say: Open the Export log tab.
steps.why: Every export is logged with the user and the time, because a report can contain personal data.

steps.say: Open Revenue by category under Accounts & Reports.
steps.why: It splits revenue by room type and the collections by payment method.
steps.expect: Revenue by category and tender opens.

steps.say: Open B. Collections by tender.
steps.why: Cash, UPI, card and bank transfer are totalled separately, so the day's money can be matched with the bank and the drawer.
steps.expect: The collections by tender are shown.

steps.say: Open C. Bridge.
steps.why: The bridge shows how the revenue figure becomes the collection figure: advances, deposits, credit and tax.
steps.expect: The bridge from revenue to collections opens.

steps.say: Sagar, the Owner, opens the Owner digest. It is the morning page: yesterday on one sheet.
steps.why: The owner reads one page a day instead of ten reports.
steps.expect: The Owner digest opens for 25 Oct 2026.

steps.say: The digest shows occupancy, revenue, collections, cash, expenses, pending approvals and exceptions for the chosen business date. Print puts it on one page, and the Outbox drafts below are the messages that would carry it to the owner by e-mail or phone.
steps.why: If a figure looks wrong, the owner asks the manager the same morning.

chapters.title: Accounting
chapters.goal: Read the vouchers HCC posts by itself, enter a contra and an owner drawing, get them approved, and read the trial balance, statements, profit and loss, balance sheet, ageing, GST, TDS, assets, Tally export, bank reconciliation and year end.

steps.say: Farhan, the Accountant, is on Modules Home. Accounting is the last stop of the money that the other chapters moved.
steps.why: Every receipt, bill and payout of the hotel already has a voucher; the accountant checks and completes them.

steps.say: Click the Accounts & Reports tile.
steps.why: Accounting sits with day closing and the reports.

steps.say: Click the Accounting tile.
steps.why: The page has one tab for every accounting job.
steps.expect: The Accounting page opens on Vouchers.

steps.say: The Vouchers tab lists the vouchers of the chosen business date: sales vouchers SAL, receipts RCT and payments PMT, each numbered with the date. HCC creates them from the folios, the cashier and the expenses; nobody types them.
steps.why: The accounts follow the hotel's work, so the books are never behind.

steps.say: Open the Manual vouchers tab.
steps.why: Entries that no screen of the hotel creates are made here by hand.
steps.expect: The manual voucher types are offered.

steps.say: Click Contra (cash and bank). The reception cash is taken to the bank.
steps.why: A contra moves money between the cash drawer and the bank without any income or expense.

steps.say: Choose From the front-desk cash, To the hotel current account, the amount 20000 and the narration: Cash taken to the bank.
steps.why: The narration says in words what the entry is, for the auditor.

steps.say: Click Send for approval.
steps.why: A manual voucher is posted only after another user approves it.

steps.say: Click Owner drawing from the bank.
steps.why: When the owner takes money out of the business, it is a drawing and not an expense.

steps.say: Choose the hotel current account, the amount 10000 and the narration: Owner drawing for personal use.
steps.why: A drawing reduces the owner's capital, not the profit.

steps.say: Click Send for approval.
steps.why: The owner approves his own drawing through the approval list, so that the record is complete.

steps.say: Sagar, the Owner, opens Accounting, Manual vouchers and the Pending approval list.
steps.why: The owner sees every manual entry before it is posted.
steps.expect: The manual vouchers with the pending ones.

steps.say: Click Pending approval.
steps.why: The list shows the contra and the drawing sent by Farhan.

steps.say: Click Approve on the first voucher, the contra.
steps.why: The approver reads the narration and the amount first; the voucher is then posted to the ledgers with its own number.
steps.expect: The contra is approved and posted.

steps.say: Click Approve on the second voucher, the owner drawing.
steps.why: Nobody approves their own entry, which is why the Owner approves what the Accountant prepared.
steps.expect: The drawing is approved and posted.

steps.say: Back as Farhan, open the GST month tab.
steps.why: The GST of the month is set off here: output tax on sales against input credit on purchases and expenses.

steps.say: Open the TDS tab.
steps.why: Tax deducted at source from contractors is recorded with the payee type and the rate, to be paid to the government by the due date.

steps.say: Open the Assets tab.
steps.why: The asset register lists furniture, machines and vehicles with their cost, date and depreciation.

steps.say: Open the Trial balance tab.
steps.why: The trial balance lists every ledger with opening, debit, credit and closing; the debits must equal the credits.

steps.say: Open the Statements tab.
steps.why: A ledger or party statement shows every entry of one account; for a company it is the statement sent for payment.

steps.say: Open the P&L tab.
steps.why: The profit and loss statement shows income, expenses and the profit of a period.
steps.expect: The profit and loss statement opens.

steps.say: Open the Balance sheet tab.
steps.why: The balance sheet shows what the hotel owns and owes on a date.

steps.say: Open the Outstanding tab.
steps.why: Ageing lists the money owed by companies and by guests in groups of days; the company credit of Shree Agro Industries is here.
steps.expect: The outstanding amounts by age are listed.

steps.say: Open the GST summary tab.
steps.why: The summary shows taxable value, CGST and SGST for each rate, ready for the return.

steps.say: Open the Cash ratio tab.
steps.why: The cash ratio compares cash takings with the total and flags an unusual share.

steps.say: Open the Exports tab.
steps.why: The Tally export writes the vouchers and the masters in the format the accountant's Tally software reads; every report can also be downloaded.

steps.say: Open the Year end tab.
steps.why: Year end closes the financial year and carries the balances forward. The training only explains it; it is never run in a demo.

steps.say: Open the Bank reconciliation tab.
steps.why: Each line of the bank statement is matched with a voucher; unmatched lines are investigated.

steps.say: Click More sections. Nine more tabs open: Clearing, Day book, Chart of accounts, Parties, Opening balances, Exceptions, Reconciliation, Mapping and Tally export.
steps.why: The rarely used pages are tucked away so that the daily tabs stay short.
steps.expect: The nine more sections are listed.

steps.say: Open the Clearing tab.
steps.why: Clearing accounts hold money in transit, such as card and UPI settlements, until the bank credits them.

steps.say: Open the Day book tab.
steps.why: The day book lists every voucher of a day in the order of posting, like the old cash book of the accountant.

steps.say: Open the Chart of accounts tab.
steps.why: The chart lists every ledger on the 28 groups of Tally; the Owner adds ledgers here.

steps.say: Open the Parties tab.
steps.why: Companies, vendors and staff have their own sub-ledgers; Shree Agro Industries owes Rs 4,725 for the stay of Vikram Jadhav.

steps.say: Open the Opening balances tab.
steps.why: The opening balances at the start of the year are entered by hand once and then locked.

steps.say: Open the Tally export tab.
steps.why: The file contains the masters and the vouchers in the format Tally reads, so the accountant never types them again.

steps.say: The Lock period button at the top is for the Owner: it locks a month after the GST return, so no entry can be added to that month. The training does not lock a month.
steps.why: A locked month protects the figures that were filed.

chapters.title: Compliance calendar and the assistant
chapters.goal: Read the compliance calendar with its Action Center and firm profile, then ask the management assistant a question and read the anomaly flags.

steps.say: Farhan is on Modules Home. Tax and licence due dates are tracked in the Compliance calendar so that none is missed.
steps.why: A missed GST or TDS date costs the hotel interest and penalty.

steps.say: Click the Accounts & Reports tile.
steps.why: The calendar and the assistant are listed next to the accounting tiles.

steps.say: Click the Compliance calendar tile.
steps.why: It lists the obligations of the financial year month by month.
steps.expect: The Compliance calendar opens on October 2026.

steps.say: October 2026 lists cards such as the TDS deposit for September, the TDS return for the second quarter, the income tax filing for audit cases and the GSTR-1 for September. Each card has its due date and its status. The tabs run April to March, and the Dashboard tab summarises the year.
steps.why: The calendar is built from the hotel's own profile, so it lists only what applies.

steps.say: Click Action Center. It shows the eleven items that need action.
steps.why: The Action Center is the short list: overdue and due-soon cards, with the amount payable worked out from HCC data.

steps.say: Click Firm profile.
steps.why: The firm profile holds the GSTIN, the registrations and the licence expiry dates that drive the calendar, including the FSSAI and lodging licence renewals.

steps.say: Press Escape to close the profile.
steps.why: Nothing changes until you save.

steps.say: Open the Dashboard tab.
steps.why: The dashboard shows the count of obligations by status for the year.

steps.say: Look at the buttons CSV register, Print month, Evidence ZIP, GSTR-1 working summary and CA pack.
steps.why: The CA pack and the evidence zip give the accountant everything for the filing in one file; evidence files are attached to each card.
steps.expect: The export buttons are on the page.

steps.say: Open Management assistant under Accounts & Reports. Sagar, the Owner, asks it questions about the hotel.
steps.why: The assistant answers from the hotel's own data; it does not use the internet.

steps.say: The page has a conversation box, suggested questions, the daily briefing and the anomaly flags. The suggested questions include Occupancy today, Next 7 days, Collections vs outstanding, Cash drawer, Pending approvals, Day-close readiness and Compliance due.
steps.why: A question can be asked by clicking, so nobody has to remember the words.

steps.say: Click Occupancy today.
steps.why: The answer is worked out from the live room board.
steps.expect: The assistant answers with today's occupancy.

steps.say: Type your own question: How full are we tomorrow?
steps.why: The assistant understands a short question in plain English.

steps.say: Click Ask.
steps.why: The reply shows the number and the rooms behind it, with a Go there link to the screen.

steps.say: Click Daily briefing.
steps.why: The briefing is the owner's morning summary in a few lines.

steps.say: The Anomaly flags list unusual things: a big discount, many voids, a large cash difference, an advance that was never used. Each flag has Go there, which opens the screen to look at it.
steps.why: The flags point at the entries worth a second look, so the owner needs no search.

chapters.title: Administration and setup
chapters.goal: Create a user and a role, switch a sub-function off and on, read the Master configuration and the room master, check approvals, take a backup, read system health, the legacy import and the roadmap.

steps.say: Sagar, the Owner, is on Modules Home. Admin & Setup holds users, roles, settings, backups and system health. Only the Owner and the Tech admin see all of it.
steps.why: What is set here changes the behaviour of every other chapter.

steps.say: Click the Admin & Setup tile.
steps.why: The module lists its pages as tiles.

steps.say: The tiles are Administration, Approvals & audit, Master configuration, Backup & recovery, System health, Legacy import, Roadmap and Appearance & display. A person with fewer rights sees fewer tiles.
steps.why: The tile list is itself a permission check.

steps.say: Click the Administration tile.
steps.why: Users, roles and the module switches are managed here.
steps.expect: Administration opens on the Users tab.

steps.say: The tabs are Modules & features, Roles, Users and Audit. Users lists the twelve demo users with Edit and Disable. In the production system each user has a PIN or password of their own; the demo has none.
steps.why: Disabling a user stops their access at once and keeps their history.

steps.say: Click New user. Sunil Pawar joined as a room attendant.
steps.why: A person gets a login only when they need one.
steps.expect: The Create a demo user dialog opens.

steps.say: Type the name Sunil Pawar and choose the role Housekeeper.
steps.why: The role decides which tiles and which actions the person has.

steps.say: Click Create user.
steps.why: The production server issues a starting PIN that the person must change at the first sign-in; the demo shows none.

steps.say: Open the Roles tab.
steps.why: Custom roles are built from a base role such as Manager and then adjusted per sub-function: Off, View or Full.
steps.expect: The roles with their permission grids open.

steps.say: Click New role.
steps.why: A hotel can have roles of its own, like the Day shift manager and the Night shift manager already here.
steps.expect: The New custom role dialog opens.

steps.say: Type the role name Night manager, keep the base role Manager and click Create role.
steps.why: The new role starts as a copy of Manager; the Owner then switches rights off one by one.

steps.say: Click Create role.
steps.why: The role appears in the list and can be given to users.

steps.say: Open the Modules & features tab.
steps.why: Each module and its sub-functions can be switched off when the hotel does not use them; the data is kept.
steps.expect: The modules and sub-functions are listed with their switches.

steps.say: Click Switch off Reservations.
steps.why: The page and the commands of the sub-function disappear for everybody; core functions such as the folio cannot be switched off.
steps.expect: Reservations is switched off and the data is kept.

steps.say: Aarav, the receptionist, opens Front Desk. The Reservations and Calendar tiles are gone; booking commands would be refused.
steps.why: A switched-off sub-function leaves no half-working screen behind.
steps.expect: The Front Desk page has no Reservations or Calendar tile.

steps.say: Sagar opens Modules & features again and clicks Switch on Reservations.
steps.why: Switching on restores the screens at once, with all the data as it was.

steps.say: Open the Audit tab.
steps.why: Every change of a role or a switch is a policy version with the user and the time.

steps.say: Open Master configuration under Admin & Setup. It holds all the settings of the hotel in twelve groups.
steps.why: Settings are in one place, grouped by the job they belong to.

steps.say: The groups are Property and branding, Rooms and rate plans, Front-desk policies, Money and tax, Restaurant and POS, Housekeeping and maintenance, People, payroll and leave, Compliance obligations, Modules on/off, Users, roles and PINs, Messages and documents, Internet access and Data and system.
steps.why: Each group shows how many settings it holds and the key values.

steps.say: Click Money and tax.
steps.why: GST rates, currency and rounding are Owner-only: a manager sees them but cannot change them. Rates are dated, so a change from a future date never alters old bills.
steps.expect: The money and tax settings open.

steps.say: Click Rooms and rate plans.
steps.why: This group holds the masters: floors, amenities, room types, rooms, occupancy charges and meal plans.
steps.expect: The lists of the group open.

steps.say: Click Rooms, 24 rooms.
steps.why: The room master lists every room with the number of stays it has had.
steps.expect: The room master opens with the 24 rooms.

steps.say: The room master offers Paste rows for a CSV import, Add rooms, Renumber and Set out of order, and the filters Active, Retired and All. Every master of the hotel can be exported and imported as a CSV file from a template.
steps.why: Imports are checked row by row before anything is saved.

steps.say: Click room 203 to open its record.
steps.why: The record holds the type, floor and amenities of the room.

steps.say: Open Internet access in the list of groups.
steps.why: Internet is Off by default; HCC works on the local network and only uses the internet for messages and the booking site if the Owner allows it.
steps.expect: The Internet access group opens: Internet is Off and guest messaging is Off.

steps.say: Open Approvals & audit under Admin & Setup and its Audit log tab.
steps.why: The audit log is the record of who did what.

steps.say: Open Backup & recovery. Click Run simulated backup.
steps.why: A backup is a copy of the hotel data kept away from the computer; the demo simulates it.

steps.say: Click Run simulated backup.
steps.why: The history shows the time and the size; a restore drill proves that a backup can really be restored.
steps.expect: A backup is added to the history.

steps.say: Open the Restore procedure tab.
steps.why: The seven steps of a restore are written down here and practised once a quarter.

steps.say: Open System health.
steps.why: System health shows stuck background work, the last backups, the internet status and the printers.

steps.say: Parked events are jobs that failed and wait for a retry. The page also shows the last backups, the internet (egress) status and the printers with a Print test page button.
steps.why: The Owner and the Tech admin look here when something does not arrive.

steps.say: Open Legacy import.
steps.why: Old guest records of the Lodge software can be loaded here, once.

steps.say: The import has a Run dry run button and a list of runs. A dry run reads the files and reports what would be loaded, per financial year, without changing anything. The training only explains it; the import is a one-time job done with the Owner.
steps.why: A dry run catches problems before any data is changed.

steps.say: Open Roadmap.
steps.why: The roadmap shows what is planned next in HCC.

steps.say: Lata, the Tech admin, signs in. She sees only People & Payroll and Admin & Setup: users, backup, system health and settings, and no hotel money.
steps.why: The Tech admin keeps the system running without access to the guest or money data.
steps.expect: Modules Home for Lata with two tiles.

chapters.title: Closing: shortcuts, help, quick-reference
chapters.goal: Learn the function keys and the shortcut list, use search once more, open your own menu for help and sign-out, and keep the quick-reference card.

steps.say: You are Aarav on Modules Home again. The last chapter is about speed: keys that take you straight to the screens you use all day.
steps.why: A receptionist who knows the keys serves the next guest sooner.

steps.say: Press Alt and the slash key to open the list of keyboard shortcuts.
steps.why: The list always shows the keys your role may use.

steps.say: The list shows the keys: F2 New booking, F3 Arrivals & check-in, F4 In-house stays, F6 Room board, F7 Guests & folios, F8 Check-out, F9 Rate / guest change, F10 Cashier shift, Alt+B Counter bill and Alt+/ this list. A key only works when you may use that screen and no dialog is open.
steps.why: Keys that you may not use are not listed for you.

steps.say: Press Escape to close the list.
steps.why: Escape closes every dialog.

steps.say: Press F6.
steps.why: F6 goes to the Room board from any screen.

steps.say: Press F3.
steps.why: F3 goes to Arrivals & check-in.

steps.say: Press Control and K to search from anywhere. Search is the other way to jump: type a part of a page name.
steps.why: Together, the keys and the search take you to any screen within two keystrokes.

steps.say: Press Escape.
steps.why: Nothing is lost by closing the search.

steps.say: Click your own name at the top right: Aarav, Reception.
steps.why: This is your own menu: change my password or PIN, display mode, sign out and about this build.

steps.say: The menu lets you change your own PIN, pick the display mode Auto, Desktop or Mobile for this device, see the build information and Sign out. Always sign out when you leave the desk, so nobody works under your name.
steps.why: Everything done in HCC is recorded under the name of the signed-in person.

steps.say: Quick reference. Modules Home: pick a module. Ctrl K: search. F2 new booking, F3 arrivals, F4 in-house, F6 room board, F7 folios, F8 check-out, F10 cashier. Esc closes a dialog. Ask the Manager for approvals, the Owner for credit notes and credit limits. Nothing in the demo is real money or a real guest.
steps.why: Keep this card at the desk; the role cards of the training give the same facts for every role.
